meta.refinement: Fill and foreground roles split; text targets raised from AA 4.5:1 to AAA 7:1; --border-strong added for WCAG 1.4.11; UEC given a third -ui variant; type scale rebased for the 50-75 bracket.

color.note: Dark is the default — @ocr/ui declares the dark roles on bare :root. Read the roles in two families: FILL roles (--accent, --live, --danger, --warn) are grounds and only need 3:1; INK roles (--text, --text-muted, --accent-text, --error, --live-text, --warn-text) are read and clear AA (4.5:1) on every ground — AA everywhere, decided 2026-09-29. A token is never both. That one split is what fixes the system.

tokens.name: map-ground
tokens.usage: The map panel's ground — deliberately identical to --bg. Every candidate map tint tested landed at 1.02-1.04:1 against --bg: invisible. The panel is marked by a --border-strong edge instead.

tokens.name: map-cell-line
tokens.usage: H3 corridor cell stroke. 3.60:1 on --bg, against 1.63:1 for the old --border stroke. An EMPTY cell is stroke-only — a --surface fill on --bg is 1.20:1 and will never read.

tokens.usage: 2px casing drawn under every map label and overlay stroke so it survives over basemap imagery. Dark casing under light text; the light theme uses --map-halo-light.

type.note: No webfonts — a poster must render instantly on a cheap phone on venue wifi. The scale is rebased for readers aged 50-75: controls and body sit at 16px, nothing drops below 13px, and error text is never smaller than body. @ocr/ui already used 16px on .search-bar and .sort-select to stop iOS zooming on focus; that was the right value for the wrong reason, and it is now the rule.

styles.name: stat-value
styles.usage: 28px, was 24px. The number in a .stat-card. Coloured --accent-text, not --accent. Tabular figures.

styles.name: page-title
styles.usage: 22px, was 20px. The h1 in .header. One per screen, always.

styles.name: section-heading
styles.usage: 20px, was 17.6px. The h3 in an .empty-state or gate.

styles.name: cta
styles.usage: 20px. Read from across a room on a venue display.

styles.name: body
styles.sample: Doors at 6, music at 7. Bring a chair.
styles.usage: 16px, was 14.4px. Running text and list names. 1.5 leading — long lines are harder to track with an ageing eye.

styles.name: button
styles.usage: 18px/700, was 14.4px/600. Sized up deliberately: at 18px bold the label counts as large text, so black on the CARTO-blue fill (5.78:1) clears the AAA threshold of 4.5:1 without repainting the brand. The primary action should also simply be the biggest label on the screen. Sentence case, and it names what happens — 'Make the poster', never 'Submit'.

styles.name: label
styles.usage: 16px, was 14px. Field labels and checkbox rows. Written as a question a neighbour would ask.

styles.name: input
styles.usage: 16px, was 13.6px. Also the value that stops iOS zooming the page on focus — a zoom that loses an older user their place in the form.

styles.name: error
styles.sample: That email is missing its ending — try hello@maplefair.org
styles.usage: 16px, was 12px. Errors are never the smallest text on the screen. The person reading this one already made a mistake and needs it most.

styles.name: hint
styles.sample: Why we ask: it sets your corridor.
styles.usage: 15px, was 12px. .form-hint. Shown before the field is touched, not after it fails.

styles.name: section-title
styles.usage: 14px, was 12.8px. One of three uppercase styles in the system.

styles.name: nav-label
styles.usage: 13px, was 10.4px, and now 600 weight. Always present — a glyph never travels alone.

styles.name: brand
styles.usage: 13px, was 11.2px. The uppercase label that stands in for a logo. There is no logo asset.

spacing.note: Only --tap-min is a variable in @ocr/ui; the rest are literals the stylesheet repeats. Two are new, and both exist for hands that shake: --tap-gap and --tap-min-primary.

tokens.name: tap-min
tokens.usage: Minimum height and width of anything touchable (--tap-min). Well above the WCAG 2.5.5 AAA floor of 44px.

tokens.name: tap-min-primary
tokens.usage: NEW. The primary action on a screen, and every control in a wizard step. Bigger because it is the one thing we want hit first time.

tokens.name: tap-gap
tokens.usage: NEW. Minimum clear space BETWEEN two touch targets. Target size alone does not prevent mis-taps — adjacency does. Destructive controls get 24px and never sit beside a primary action.

tokens.name: page-pad-x
tokens.usage: Left and right padding on .content, .header, .page-header.

tokens.name: page-pad-y
tokens.usage: Vertical padding on sticky chrome.

tokens.name: section-gap
tokens.usage: Space below a .section — the page's one rhythm.

tokens.name: card-pad
tokens.usage: Padding inside .card, raised from 14px so the larger type is not crowded against the edge.

tokens.name: stack-gap
tokens.usage: Gap between siblings inside a card or empty state.

tokens.name: inline-gap
tokens.usage: Gap between a control's glyph and its label.

tokens.name: field-gap
tokens.usage: Gap between a field's label, control, hint and error, raised from 6px.

tokens.name: content-bottom
tokens.usage: Bottom padding on .content so the fixed .bottom-nav never covers the last row.

radius.note: Three variables plus three literals. The system has no shadows, so radius and a line are the only things that say 'separate object'.

tokens.name: radius-sm
tokens.usage: --radius-sm, the default: cards, buttons, inputs, list rows.

tokens.name: radius
tokens.usage: --radius: drop zones and blocks that hold a whole section.

tokens.name: radius-pill
tokens.usage: --radius-pill: chips, badges, the live indicator.

tokens.name: radius-xs
tokens.usage: Literal 4px: .bar-track and .bar-fill — barely rounded, so a bar still reads as a measurement.

tokens.name: radius-control
tokens.usage: Literal 6px: .view-btn, .track-art.

tokens.name: radius-round
tokens.usage: Literal 50%: .spinner, .profile-avatar, the toggle knob.
